newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bank of Israel chief warns against raising taxes.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Israel chief warns against raising taxes.

text.p: Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel said that raising taxes instead cutting the budget next year would not revive economic growth or improve the country's balance of payments.

"The reduction of the budget deficit must come from reducing expenses and not by raising taxes, because only (the latter) will lead to a real devaluation (of the shekel) that is so important to the business sector," Frenkel told the newspaper Haaretz.
His remarks followed a meeting on Sunday of the parliamentary finance committee, where legislators indicated they would oppose a Treasury plan to impose fees for doctor appointments.

An adviser to the committee said the panel was likely to vote against the fees, which together with a proposed 25 percent rise in drug prices were supposed to bring in 500 million shekels in revenues next year.
Legislators instead proposed, among other things, raising the value-added tax, levies of cigarettes and petrol, and increasing employer social security contributions.
The budget, which must be approved by parliament by December 31, has met strong opposition in parliament on the grounds that spending cuts will hit lower-income groups hardest.
